meaning: Titles and reading notes drafted by an AI agent in the register of the paper they annotate. No mathematician has reviewed them.

notes.Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace: One energy bound must hold for the excluded global smooth solution at every nonnegative time.
notes.Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus: The periodic obstruction concerns unit-periodic velocity on Euclidean space and contains no quantitative convergence rate.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellSystem.CellSystem: The fractional cell condition has twelve clauses at α=501/500, separate from the classical fifteen-clause condition.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellSystem.fractional: The fractional cell result fixes α=501/500 and uses its separate twelve-clause condition.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond: All fifteen conditions refer to the same seven groups of data and remain hypotheses of the conditional breakdown theorem.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpa: The theorem combines the two conditional breakdown conclusions. It does not construct numerical data satisfying the cell conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert: A suitable decay constant is chosen existentially; all the other certificate data are retained.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.spaceBreakdown: The completed whole-space argument supplies the analytic estimates and retains all fifteen cell conditions on the given data.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedSigmaProfileOfHel: The existence conclusion omits equations identifying the output profile with the selected parameter and correction.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.GraphClosedHolds: Each element of the closed graph has the required relation between its gradient and second-derivative components.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.ReadingEnergyHolds: The physical representation identifies the weighted energy, gradient norm and pin pairings with the corresponding Fourier quantities.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol: The zero-multiplier argument chooses a parameter after the fixed-parameter nonlinear correction has been constructed.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldExistsUniqueH: Uniqueness holds within the set of allowed corrections at a fixed parameter. It makes no uniqueness claim about arbitrary Navier–Stokes solutions.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHel: The proof constructs the profile from the selected parameter and correction, while the displayed existence conclusion omits those equalities.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.extended_certificate_orbi: Normalization of multiplier weight and absorption of the model-to-profile gap prepare the extended certificate for the fixed-point argument.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.halfSsp_of_xbar: Membership in the closed graph implies the half-order Fourier derivative relation used to identify the physical energy.
notes.Breakdown.Cert.readingEnergyHolds_of: The energy and pin identities follow from the derivative relation for every element of the closed Fourier graph.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.cellLayerParts_closed: The theorem supplies the analytic cell estimates and retains the numerical entry conditions in their hypotheses.
notes.Breakdown.DichotomyHolds: The spectral splitting has a finite-dimensional exceptional range, forward decay, backward bounds and surjectivity on that range.
notes.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.toCert: The conversion reuses earlier operator coordinates and sets several unused quantities to zero. It supplies no assertion that the converted data meet the earlier certificate conditions.
notes.Breakdown.FarField.SmoothFieldOfOrbit: The input period and isometry are retained, and the smooth field agrees with the orbit almost everywhere in space at every time.
notes.Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileE: The final existence statement omits the selected weak-to-smooth field correspondence; the internal smoothing theorem retains it.
notes.Breakdown.FarField.smoothFieldOfOrbit_ho: The smooth representative has the same period and isometry as the orbit and represents it almost everywhere in space at each time.
notes.Breakdown.FieldReading: The recovered L⁶ velocity is injective as a representation of the Fourier state and respects rotations and dilations.
notes.Breakdown.Freq.EmbedLinear: The embedding preserves addition, subtraction and real scalar multiplication on smooth decaying fields.
notes.Breakdown.Freq.EmbedNorm: For smooth decaying fields, the squared Fourier-space norm equals the sum of the squared L² norms of the three physical coordinate derivatives.
notes.Breakdown.Freq.embedNormLinear_holds: The theorem contains both the norm identity and linearity; the first conclusion supplies the norm identification.
notes.Breakdown.Freq.realization: The construction realizes the evolution through gradient-weighted Fourier fields and supplies their physical interpretation.
notes.Breakdown.Held.testSetZero: Compactness and convexity of the parameter set, together with the specified boundary conditions, support the finite-dimensional zero argument.
notes.Breakdown.MildRegular: On every fixed closed time interval, a suitable mild flow has smooth physical velocity and pressure with the stated energy and gradient bounds.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.MovingFrameReduction: A moving frame removes the affine nonperiodic pressure part while preserving the initial datum.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup: The internal result retains a mild torus trajectory whose norm is unbounded before the terminal time.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p: The smooth recurrent-profile hypothesis is carried through the torus construction and the smooth-versus-mild uniqueness comparison.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.movingFrameReduction: The pressure drift is integrated twice, with zero initial frame shift and velocity, so the transformed datum stays unchanged.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.torusBlowup_of_parts: The construction combines approximation, right-inverse transfer, perturbation and gluing, retaining the stated analytic hypotheses.
notes.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: The recurrent profile has spatial derivative bounds through order two and cubic pressure-gradient decay, in addition to smoothness, recurrence and nonzero velocity.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.fracCertificate_pro: The fractional certificate supplies a rotating fractional profile through its own regularity and decay argument.
notes.Breakdown.TransferHolds: For data in any prescribed dense subspace, the statement keeps a positive power-law rate of convergence to the recurrent profile in similarity variables.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.WeakOrbitOfParts: The output asserts existence of an orbit, period and twist. It does not state the full correspondence with the originally supplied weak field.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.weakOrbitOfParts_h: The construction uses the original period and twist and a continuous representative of the weak field; the final existence statement hides that correspondence.
notes.Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_weak: The weak profile first gives a recurrent mild orbit, to which the common whole-space transfer argument is applied.
notes.Breakdown.dichotomyHolds: The theorem establishes the compact-perturbation spectral splitting used in the transfer construction.
notes.Breakdown.exists_blowup_datum: This intermediate theorem retains the mild trajectory, recurrent orbit and convergence rate that the final obstruction does not state.
notes.Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_pro: The completed extended-certificate argument supplies the analytic estimates and returns existence of a weak recurrent profile.
notes.Breakdown.fieldReading_realization: The theorem establishes injectivity and rotational and dilation covariance for the physical velocity of the Fourier evolution.
notes.Breakdown.fractional_breakdown_on_space: The fractional implication assumes a rotating profile with dissipation exponent strictly between one and five quarters.
notes.Breakdown.fractional_breakdown_on_torus: The periodic fractional implication has the same open exponent range and belongs to the separate fractional equation family.
notes.Breakdown.mildRegular_realization: The proof uses the heat, bilinear and H¹ identities to construct the smooth physical representative.
notes.Breakdown.transferHolds_of: The transfer argument chooses initial data in the prescribed dense subspace and retains the power-law convergence estimate.
notes.Breakdown.transferHolds_of_dichotomy: This transfer proof supplies the intermediate evolution estimates while retaining the spectral dichotomy as an explicit hypothesis.
